pr: Before designing anything, audit the problem: who loses photos, where, and why?
ai: Mapped three personas: Ravi on the roof, Sean in the office, Priya handling claims.
me: Framed the whole project as one problem: photos from the roof to the office.

pr: Research each persona’s working day so the journey map is grounded in real work.
ai: Desk research on crew days, PM days and adjuster photo expectations.
me: Kept research to what changes the design.

pr: The inspector already photographs the damage. Why does the persona say the photos live on someone else’s phone?
ai: Had merged inspection and repair photos into one set.
me: Separated the two: repair proof comes only from the crew.

pr: Which photo stages does an insurance adjuster actually expect to see?
me: Settled on three per spot: Before, Opened up, Fixed.

pr: Seven photo states are too many for anyone to remember. Please simplify.
me: Kept two meanings that matter: on the phone, or in the office.

pr: Please remove the alert timers and escalation rules.
ai: Designed four-hour escalations and alert cancellation logic.
me: Too deep for the brief. Discarded.

pr: Please remove the lost-photo ownership workflow.
ai: Wrote rules for who records an unrecoverable photo.
me: An edge case, not the core problem. Discarded.

pr: Before building, check every flow against the problem statement.
ai: Added a problem-statement audit to each step.
me: Made this a standing rule.

pr: Design our own app from the start rather than extending the current Zuper app.
me: Company, then email and password, then home.

pr: Start with wireframes, working left to right from the login screen.
me: Wireframes before visuals.

pr: Why do we show “Ready for offline” at sign-in?
ai: Added an offline-readiness screen at login.
me: Offline should be invisible until it matters.

pr: Please remove clock-in.
ai: Included a clock-in and timesheet flow.
me: Payroll and hours sit outside this problem. Discarded.

pr: Add a check-in so the office knows when the crew is on site.
ai: Started the job at the first photo.
me: Check-in became the start of every job.

pr: The flow between photos, work and finishing the job is broken. Please fix it.
ai: Jumped from arrival photos straight to finish.
me: Added the missing work and check-out steps.

pr: Make sure every count adds up across all screens.
ai: Counts differed between crew and office views.
me: One job, #421, runs through all three apps.

pr: Review Mobbin for a visual direction that suits roofing crews.
me: Strong type and high contrast for outdoor use.

pr: The contrast fails outdoors. Please make it readable in sunlight.
me: Ink on white, colour only for meaning.

pr: Move away from heavy rounded corners towards a more professional style.
me: Tighter radii and a calmer surface.

pr: The reference photo is too large. Capture should feel fast.
ai: Showed a large example photo per shot.
me: Smaller reference, faster capture.

pr: Use a list instead; the grid only fits four items.
ai: Laid out shots as a card grid.
me: A list that scales to any job.

pr: The slope selector reads like a set of photo filters.
me: Plain labels; added a flash control.

pr: Please remove voice tagging.
me: Unreliable on a noisy roof. Discarded.

pr: Please remove the AI “too close” coaching overlay.
me: Added noise without solving the core gap. Discarded.

pr: Why are two arrival photos already filled in?
me: Every state starts empty and truthful.

pr: Red reads as an error here. Please use a different colour.
me: Red only for real risk.

pr: Repair photos must be taken in order.
me: Each spot unlocks in sequence.

pr: What is the real difference between Before, Opened up and Fixed?
ai: Treated the three as one burst.
me: Shoot each at its moment in the repair.

pr: If I take six photos quickly, I lose track of which label I am on.
ai: Kept the label small above the shutter.
me: Clear label and stepper in the camera.

pr: Please remove the “before you touch it” note.
ai: Repeated guidance on the job screen.
me: Crew won't read it mid-job. Discarded.

pr: Why are there three actions on this screen?
me: One primary action per screen.

pr: The steps after starting work vary by job. Please make them universal.
me: A vertical timeline anyone can follow.

pr: There is a gap between the arrival photos and the repair. Should Ravi tap “Start work”?
ai: Went from arrival straight to Spot A.
me: Added Start work so Sean knows work began.

pr: Tapping “Start work” feels like nothing happened. Please give clear feedback.
me: A short confirmation, then the next step.

pr: “Before” looks like a button.
ai: Filled the current stage in black.
me: Black reserved for actions.

pr: Should the crew be able to delete a photo after it has uploaded?
me: No delete once in the office.

pr: Does Ravi really need Home, Jobs and Uploads?
me: Two tabs: My jobs and Uploads.

pr: Please remove the Today and Tomorrow tabs.
me: One vertical list of jobs.

pr: How do we know the job is 2.4 miles away?
me: Removed data the app can't know.

pr: “Starts in 10 min” reads like a movie ticket.
me: Show the start time.

pr: The gate code does not belong on the job card.
ai: Listed gate code on the list.
me: Only what Ravi needs to choose a job.

pr: Check-in belongs in the job details.
ai: Put Check in on the list card.
me: He sees the job before checking in.

pr: Should the address or the customer name come first?
me: Address first; name second.

pr: No signal is the core case, not an edge case.
me: Built a separate no-signal version.

pr: Show no signal as a simple pill rather than a banner.
me: A small amber pill, then it goes.

pr: The Uploads screen should explain where each photo is.
me: Per-job rows with a bottom sheet.

pr: The directions button should not be green.
me: Green only means 'in office'.

pr: Will Ravi shoot in portrait or landscape?
me: Landscape suits roofs and reports.

pr: Do not make Ravi rotate his phone.
ai: Asked him to turn the phone.
me: Portrait UI, fixed 4:3 frame.

pr: The job header is too tall.
me: Four compact facts in boxes.

pr: Make the check-out moment clear.
me: A green check-out panel, next job removed.

pr: What is Sean’s main job in the web app?
me: Fix photo gaps and answer customer requests.

pr: This cannot be a dashboard when there are 20 requests.
ai: One large card for one customer.
me: A request queue that scales.

pr: Show an overview rather than everything at once.
ai: Packed every signal into one section.
me: Separate, quiet sections.

pr: Customer requests are the main flow.
me: Gutter complaint first; photo gaps as alerts.

pr: “Needs action” should take the full row.
me: Full-width Needs action, two sections below.

pr: Section titles do not need numbers.
me: Titles only.

pr: “9 things need you” is too casual.
me: Professional, plain labels.

pr: Who creates the data in “Needs action”?
ai: Implied the system knew the complaint.
me: Photo rows are automatic; requests are logged by people.

pr: Use the job number instead of 1, 2, 3.
me: #421 as the row ID.

pr: The customer request needs more focus than the photo risk.
me: Amber request pill; red only for photos at risk.

pr: “Opened up photo not taken” is confusing.
me: Clear stage names and short status.

pr: What does “Ravi last heard” mean?
me: Plain 'phone synced' wording.

pr: Please remove the chat with Ravi.
me: No signal on the roof. Discarded.

pr: Would a phone call work better than a message?
me: Call kept; it works on weak signal.

pr: AI should draft a reply only when Sean asks for one.
me: A 'Draft reply' button, same as Priya.

pr: Do not label search as AI.
me: Search just works, with a thinking state.

pr: Search results should have their own page.
me: Dropdown to jump; full page for results.

pr: How can AI help on the job page?
me: One check: what was asked, what we have.

pr: AI photo picking and manual photo picking should not be two separate paths.
me: AI preselects; Sean can change any pick.

pr: Why do we explain to Sean why the insurer needs photos?
me: Hidden; it's Priya's concern.

pr: The reply should feel like writing an email.
me: A familiar mail composer.

pr: Please remove the “Not sent” label.
me: Noise; drafts simply aren't sent. Discarded.

pr: After sending, the page still says “Share 3 photos”.
me: The page closes the request.

pr: Do we need notifications for everything?
me: A bell in both web apps.

pr: Who is the adjuster in this flow?
me: Adjuster: the insurer's person who reviews the claim.

pr: What does Priya check before she sends a claim?
me: Ready, missing, or needs a note.

pr: “Check package” is not a clear action label.
me: 'Review'.

pr: Success should not be a static state.
me: A top-right snackbar.

pr: Show the AI working while it drafts.
me: A short analysing sequence, then writing.

pr: Keep only the essential information.
me: Cut to what she sends.

pr: Zuper owns the product; Halden is the client.
me: Zuper logo, Halden as the workspace.

pr: Make the buttons sleeker for web.
me: Smaller primary and secondary styles.

pr: Separate the job title from its details.
me: White header, grey detail panel.

pr: Create one entry point for all three flows.
me: Sean, Priya and app flow from one page.

pr: When signed in as Sean, show only Sean’s view.
me: One user per prototype.

pr: Remove the unified dashboard for both roles.
ai: One sidebar for Sean and Priya.
me: Different jobs, different homes. Discarded.

pr: The primary colour must match across both apps.
ai: Used a new palette on mobile.
me: One palette everywhere.

pr: The AI card must match Priya’s styling.
me: One AI style.

pr: Should the top search bar be sticky?
me: Sticky on every page.

pr: Centre the search and remove the “H” logo.
me: Centred search, cleaner bar.

pr: This looks generic and AI-generated. Please give it more character.
me: Plain, editorial cover.

pr: Remove the preview strip under the hero.
me: The flows show themselves. Discarded.

pr: This should be a hero cover, not a detail page.
me: A case-study cover.

pr: The author credit is getting lost.
me: Clear 'Thageer Ashraf' credit.

pr: Remove Halden from the cover.
me: Cover is about the assignment. Discarded.

pr: Use real device photos for each flow.
me: Our screens on real devices.

pr: Keep a log of every prompt.
me: A full log with intent and outcome.

pr: Make the log easy for an interviewer to read.
me: Summary first, full log last.

pr: The key decisions table is empty.
ai: Lost the data in an edit.
me: Restored and checked.

pr: Tell the process as a story.
me: 100 decisions from research to cover.
